question: CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) ⇌ CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g); ΔH = -890 kJ mol⁻¹. If pressure is increased according to Le Chatelier's principle the equilibrium state—
options: [{"label":"a","text":"Will shift to the right side","is_correct":true},{"label":"b","text":"Will shift to the left side","is_correct":false},{"label":"c","text":"Has no effect on equilibrium state","is_correct":false},{"label":"d","text":"Heat is decreased","is_correct":false}]
explanation:
Counting gas moles: Left side = 1 + 2 = 3 moles; Right side = 1 + 2 = 3 moles. Wait, if H₂O is gas, both sides have 3 moles. However, if H₂O is liquid (which is more typical): Left = 3 moles, Right = 1 mole. Increasing pressure favors the side with fewer gas moles (right side).
Correction: The state of H₂O matters. If H₂O(g): no effect (answer c). If H₂O(l): shift right (answer a). Combustion typically produces H₂O(l), so answer should be a) shift right.
